title: 闻王昌龄左迁龙标遥有此寄
titlePy: Wén Wáng Chānglíng Zuǒ Qiān Lóng Biāo Yáo Yǒu Cǐ Jì
titleEn: Hearing That Wang Changling Has Been Demoted to Longbiao, I Send This from Afar
author: 李白
intro: Li Bai hears that his friend, the poet Wang Changling, has been sent away to a remote post. He cannot go with him, so he gives his worried heart to the moon and asks it to follow his friend all the way there.
analysis: 王昌龄是李白的好朋友，也是著名诗人。他被降职到偏远的龙标（今湖南怀化一带），李白听说后写了这首诗寄给他。第一句写景：杨花已经落完，杜鹃鸟在不停地叫。暮春时节，花落了，春天要走了；杜鹃的叫声又凄凉，传说像在说“不如归去”。景色里已经带着离别的哀伤。第二句交代事情：听说你去龙标，要经过五条溪水——路途遥远又艰难。后两句是全诗最有名的地方：我把我的愁心交给明月，让它随着风，一直陪你到夜郎以西。人不能去，就让月亮替我去。月亮无论多远都能照到，所以诗人把它当成信使。这种把感情交给景物的写法叫“托物寄情”，想象新奇，感情真挚。
analysisEn: Wang Changling was a famous poet and a good friend of Li Bai. When Li Bai heard that Wang had been demoted to Longbiao, a remote place in today’s western Hunan, he wrote this poem and sent it to him. The first line sets the scene: the willow catkins have all fallen, and the cuckoo keeps calling. It is late spring — the blossoms are gone, the season is leaving — and the cuckoo’s cry was said to sound like “better to go home”. Sadness is already in the landscape. The second line gives the news: I hear you must cross five rivers to reach Longbiao — a long, hard journey. The last two lines are the famous part: I give my worried heart to the bright moon and let it go with the wind, all the way west of Yelang. Li Bai cannot travel with his friend, so the moon will go instead; it shines everywhere, however far, so it can be his messenger. Handing your feelings to something in nature like this is a favourite device in Chinese poetry, and here it is both imaginative and sincere.
background: Li Bai (701–762) and Wang Changling (c. 698–c. 757) were close friends. Wang was demoted to Longbiao, traditionally said to be for not taking care over minor matters of conduct; the poem is usually dated to around 748–749.
pronunciation: 子规 guī；闻道 wén dào；龙标 lóng biāo；过五溪 guò；夜郎 yè láng。左迁 zuǒ qiān（降职）。
version: 采用统编教材（七年级上册）文本。“随风直到夜郎西”一作“随君直到夜郎西”；题目一作《闻王昌龄左迁龙标尉遥有此寄》。

lines.py: yáng huā luò jìn zǐ guī tí
lines.lit: Willow catkins have all fallen, the cuckoo cries;
lines.en: The willow down has all blown away; the cuckoo calls —

lines.py: wén dào lóng biāo guò wǔ xī
lines.lit: I hear that going to Longbiao you pass five streams.
lines.en: I hear the road to Longbiao crosses five wild rivers.

lines.py: wǒ jì chóu xīn yǔ míng yuè
lines.lit: I send my sorrowing heart to the bright moon,
lines.en: I give my worried heart into the moon’s keeping,

lines.py: suí fēng zhí dào yè láng xī
lines.lit: to follow the wind straight to west of Yelang.
lines.en: to ride the wind with you, all the way past Yelang.

words.note: 古代以右为尊、左为卑，所以降职叫“左迁”。现代汉语说“降职”。
唐代县名，在今湖南怀化一带；这里也指王昌龄（古人常用任职地代称人）。
柳絮，暮春时像雪一样飘飞。
杜鹃鸟的别名，现代汉语一般说“杜鹃”。
现代汉语有“啼哭”“鸡啼”，口语说“叫”。
湘西、黔东一带五条溪水的总称，代表偏远难行的地方。
给。现代汉语有“赠与”“授与”，书面语。

words.en: Yelang (a remote region in the southwest)
words.note: 古国名，在今贵州一带；成语“夜郎自大”就出自它。

imagery.name: 杜鹃
imagery.zh: 暮春里杜鹃（子规）声声啼叫，叫声凄凉，渲染出离别和贬谪的哀伤。
imagery.en: The cuckoo (子规) calling in late spring — a mournful sound that colours the scene with the sadness of parting and exile.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月亮能照到任何地方，诗人把愁心托付给它，让它代替自己陪伴朋友。
imagery.en: The moon shines everywhere, so the poet entrusts his worry to it and sends it to keep his friend company.

imagery.name: 柳
imagery.zh: 杨花（柳絮）落尽，暗示春天将尽，也带出漂泊、离别的意味。
imagery.en: The willow catkins have all fallen: spring is ending, and there is a hint of drifting and parting.
